explanation: The I47V substitution at position 47 in the flap region reduces darunavir binding through a subtle loss of van der Waals contacts rather than a dramatic conformational change. Isoleucine's larger branched aliphatic side chain makes more extensive hydrophobic interactions with darunavir at the 2.8 Å contact distance, while valine's smaller side chain diminishes these favorable van der Waals contributions in this flap-proximal binding pocket. This modest decrease in binding affinity (ΔΔG ≈ -0.2 kcal/mol) suggests the mutation achieves resistance not through steric clash avoidance, but through incremental weakening of the lipophilic network that stabilizes inhibitor positioning in this critical flap-adjacent region.
